PAGE MAP (all 12 indices accounted for): idx 0 bilingual cover; ENGLISH on the even indices 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (idx 2 instructions + Section A Q1-4; idx 4 Q5-7; idx 6 Section B Q8-11; idx 8 Q12-13 + Section C note + Q14 passage, (a)-(c) and the OR; idx 10 the Q14 OR block + Q15 with its figure, (a)-(c) and the OR); HINDI on the odd indices 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 (each opens Hindi; idx 9 opens with the Hindi Q14 OR block, so no English spills onto an odd page); idx 11 is BLANK at full size (a rule, an asterisk and the footer). The alternating hypothesis held with no parity inversion. Questions run 1-15 unbroken. STRUCTURE read off the printed General Instructions on idx 2 matches term2_s10 exactly: (i) 15 questions; (ii) three Sections A, B, C; (iii) A = Q1-7, two marks each; (iv) B = Q8-13, three marks each; (v) C = Q14 and 15 case based, four marks each; (vi) 'Internal choices have been provided in some questions' with NO count. The Section C header adds: each case has 03 sub-questions (a, b and c), (a) and (b) compulsory, internal choice in (c). Part marks: Q14 prints 1+1+2 = 4; Q15 prints only 4 and the scheme splits it 1 / 1 / 2 for both (c) branches. OR ROSTER built by walking the marking scheme for a bare OR between answer blocks and confirming each against a printed OR on the paper: Q5, Q6, Q7, Q9, Q12, Q14(c), Q15(c) = 7 alternatives. Q6's OR replaces the WHOLE of Q6 (parts (a)+(b), the scheme prints a fresh '6.' for the OR), and so do the ORs of Q7, Q9 and Q12. The ORs in the two case studies replace part (c) only; the alternative carries no printed label, so refs are Q14ca/Q14cb and Q15ca/Q15cb (Q15's (c) has its own (i)/(ii) inside, kept in one row). MARKING SCHEME: 8 pages, every page footed 'X_50_086_31/2/1_Science', cover 'Paper Code : 31/2/1': it is a PER-SET scheme for this paper alone, not a series file with sets 1-3 together. No void or award-regardless note anywhere in it. DECIMALS: ordinary baseline dots on this paper (0.01 cm, 0.5 A, checked at 3x), although its scheme writes raised ones; followed the paper. 'F1'/'F2' are printed as plain 'F1'/'F2', not subscripts, and are kept so. Opener of series 31/2: nothing skipped. No MCQs, so no answer fields.

questions.stem: “Carbon prefers to share its valence electrons with other atoms of carbon or with atoms of other elements rather than gaining or losing the valence electrons in order to attain noble gas configuration.” Give reasons to justify this statement.

questions._flag: Home is a judgement call. In the 2022 Term-II syllabus this sits with Periodic Classification (valency from electronic configuration, the nature of a metal's oxide), but every part is answerable from live content (sodium's configuration and basic metal oxides are taught in Metals and Non-metals), so it is filed on the live chapter rather than on Periodic Classification of Elements [Outdated].
questions.stem:
The atomic number of an element ‘X’ is 11.

(i) Write the electronic configurations of X and find its valency.

(ii) Write the formula and nature of its oxide.

Give reasons :

(i) Placenta is extremely essential for foetal development.

(ii) Uterine lining becomes thick and spongy after fertilisation.

(a) Name the reproductive and non-reproductive parts of bread mould (Rhizopus).

(b) List any two advantages of vegetative propagation.
Name the reproductive parts of an angiosperm. Where are these parts located ? Explain the structure of its male reproductive part.
What is puberty ? Mention any two changes that are common to both boys and girls in early teenage years.

(i) \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}\)

(ii) \(\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\)

(a) Name the functional group present in their compounds.

(b) Write the general formula for the compounds of this functional group.

(c) State the relationship between these compounds and draw the structure of any other compound having similar functional group.

(b) List two differences between the properties exhibited by covalent compounds and ionic compounds.

(b) Does a male child inherit X chromosome from his father ? Justify.

(c) How many types of gametes are produced by a human female ?
